title: Дед или собака по кличке Дед  (A Grandfather or a Dog Named Grandpa)

segments.t: Disaster nearly strikes at the bar when Sasha expresses sympathy to Vika about Kostya's dead dog right after Vika heard it was his grandfather. Thinking fast on his feet to save Max, Kostya explains to both women that his old dog was affectionately nicknamed 'Grandpa'.
И поэтому и была кличка у нее Дед.
Ты же только что Вику убрал.
Костян, да я сам не знаю.
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'Did he not tell Max?' Max asks calmly in this moment, combining "skazal" ("said") and "ne" ("not") so the key meaning lands right away.
'He was very old.' Vika chooses a firm line in the room, putting "sovsem" ("at all") alongside "staryy" ("old") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'It is a shame about his grandfather.' Kostya favors a measured posture right away, putting "zhalko" ("feel sorry for") alongside "deda" ("grandfathers") in a tight, everyday turn of phrase.
'Wait, Max said that it was a dog.' Vika sets an easygoing attitude for Max, leaning on "skazal" ("said") before closing the thought with "sobaka" ("dog").
'His grandfather? Max said that?' Vika questions promptly during the talk, using "deda" (from "ded", "grandfathers") alongside "skazal" ("said") to shape the meaning.
'She was just a very old dog.' Kostya sustains a sharp line without hesitation, linking "prosto" ("just"), "ochen" ("very much"), and "staraya" ("old") in one brisk exchange.
И поэтому и была кличка у нее Дед.
'And that is why her nickname was Grandpa.' Max presents an earnest attitude straight away, joining "poetomu" ("that's why") to "byla" ("was") so every word pulls its weight.
'I feel so sorry for Kostya.' Vika presents a steady bearing in this beat, linking "ochen" ("very much"), "zhal" ("it is a pity"), and "kosti" ("bones") in one brisk exchange.
'Already with Sasha too.' Kostya conveys a pointed approach during the exchange, joining "uzhe" ("already, now") to "sashey" ("Sasha") so every word pulls its weight.
Ты же только что Вику убрал.
'You only just got Vika out of the way.' Max chooses a brisk direction in the conversation, leaning on "tolko" ("only") before closing the thought with "ubral" ("to remove, to take away").
Костян, да я сам не знаю.
'Kostyan, I do not even know what to do myself.' Max shares a candid style beside Kostya, combining "znayu" ("know") and "kostyan" ("Kostyan") so the key meaning lands right away.
'How are they, what happened?' Kostya tests plainly for Vika's benefit, joining "kak" ("how") to "oni" ("they") so every word pulls its weight.
'Wait, what? Amazing?' Max inquires steadily at this point, leaning on "potryasayushche" ("incredible") before closing the thought with "chto" ("what").
И поэтому и была кличка у нее Дед.
Ты же только что Вику убрал.
Костян, да я сам не знаю.
That wraps up this scene as sasha and Vika compare notes about Kostya's tragedy in front of him, forcing Kostya to improvise that his late dog was nicknamed 'Grandpa'. Until next time!
